fields.why: The only continuous candidate is the median number of sex partners by vaccination status, a patient characteristic like median age (which neither reader counted); it is compared ('more sex partners'), so A's reading under the 'compared or interpreted' sentence is defensible, but the headline claims rest on proportions and case counts.

brief_issues: Section A excludes descriptive medians of population characteristics but admits a median that is compared; it does not say which wins for a compared characteristic (sex partners, age by vaccination status). A rule such as 'characteristics of who the cases are, even when compared across groups, do not make an outcome continuous' would decide it.
